image-of-text-vs-live-text-core-detectio.mechanism: Dish names are images of text delivered as a single CSS sprite-sheet background-image (no /alt), revealed per row via background-position. The .name contains no text node at all (it is empty); the accessible name is supplied by an aria-label of the actual dish name on that span (with role="text"). The brush-script presentation is achievable with a licensed @font-face webfont + live text; the names are words, not a logotype, not a picture with significant other visual content, and not user-customizable.
image-of-text-vs-live-text-core-detectio.scenario: Trattoria del Ponte dinner menu: each dish name is painted from a single SVG sprite-sheet set as a CSS background-image and revealed per row with background-position (brush-script 'calligraphy'); the .name span is empty with aria-label="<dish name>" (e.g. 'Tagliatelle al Ragù'), so AT users hear the dish but the visible name is fixed pixels; prices are live text and the live-text 'Dolci' course is the achievable foil.
image-of-text-vs-live-text-core-detectio.note: Page genuinely demonstrates the aspect, but two concrete details drifted: the markup has EMPTY <span class="name rN"> spans (no off-screen/indented real text node), and the dish name is the span's own aria-label (role="text"), not a generic aria-label="menu item" on the <li>.
